When the Referer is unavailable, Back() tries the opt-in previous URL before the fallback. This prevents an open redirect. The scheme is not compared, so Back() works behind a TLS-terminating proxy. On HTTPS, an http Referer is upgraded to https . Previous URL If a form returns Back() but the browser does not send its previous address ( Referer ), enable this option. For example, it helps when your site uses Referrer-Policy: no-referrer : After a successful page visit, a later Back() can use that saved address. Back() and the middleware's empty-response redirect look for a target in this order: 1. The same-host Referer . 2. The remembered URL. 3. The fallback. context.Inertia().PreviousUrl reads the remembered URL. It returns null when the option is disabled, or when the remembered URL is absent or invalid. The remembered URL is user-controlled input, validated as a relative path. Only successful status-200 page GET renders are remembered, including initial HTML visits. Partial reloads, prefetches, Precognition, non-GET requests and error pages are excluded. The value is the relative PathBase + Path + QueryString , without scheme or host. It is stored in the plain .Inertia.Previous session cookie. The cookie is HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , Path=/ and essential, and Secure follows o.State.CookieSecurePolicy . The cookie is written only when the URL changes. Set o.State.PreviousUrlCookieName to change the cookie name. The name must differ from o.State.CookieName . The .Inertia.Previous cookie is used with both cookie and session state stores. It is per browser, not per tab : the most recent page render wins across tabs. The Referer still takes precedence when available. What the middleware changes Situation Result --- --- 302 for PUT, PATCH, DELETE or QUERY Changed to 303 See Other , so the browser follows with a GET Redirect to another origin, non-prefetch 409 with X-Inertia-Location : the client makes a full visit instead of an XHR the browser would block Redirect whose Location contains , non-prefetch 409 with X-Inertia-Redirect : the client performs a full visit that keeps the fragment Location(url) 409 + X-Inertia-Location for Inertia requests, a plain 302 otherwise Empty 200 response Redirect back (302, or 303 for PUT/PATCH/DELETE/QUERY), using the same previous-URL and app-root fallback as Back() Vary Vary: X-Inertia is added to every response through the middleware Turn off external redirect conversion with o.ConvertExternalRedirects = false if the app intentionally redirects to another origin. Pages without a handler MapInertia maps GET and HEAD to Render("About", props) , like Laravel's Route::inertia . In MVC, return this.InertiaView(props); renders the action's own component. The default component name is {Controller}/{Action} . AddInertiaMvc(o = o.ComponentResolver = ctx = ...) changes the rule. History encryption encryptHistory is written as true only when set and is not carried across redirects. The Inertia client encrypts its history state with the page's key. Clearing history clearHistory goes through the state store. It applies to the next page rendered after the redirect(s), and is then consumed. It is typically used before a redirect after logout. Preserving a fragment By default a redirect loses the URL fragment. PreserveFragment() keeps it across the next redirect. The client receives preserveFragment: true on the next page. Page URL The page object's url is PathBase, Path and QueryString. If your app runs behind a proxy that rewrites paths, set o.UrlResolver to return the URL that the browser sees: Flash data, errors, clearHistory and preserveFragment share the state store. By default the state store is an encrypted cookie. See Flash data.

title: Deferred props
description: Load slow page sections after the first render, in groups.
body: Defer leaves a prop out of the first response and lists it under deferredProps . The client requests each group with a partial reload as soon as the page is mounted. The page becomes interactive without waiting for the slow data. A deferred prop can also be live. A live deferred prop is fetched again whenever its event is broadcast. Props in the same group load in one request. Different groups load in parallel requests. Inertia.Net only produces deferredProps on non-partial renders. The client The fallback is a prop in React, a fallback slot in Vue and a fallback snippet in Svelte. Combining with other props A deferred prop can also be merged, once or rescued: The metadata combines: deferredProps lists the group, mergeProps lists the path, and onceProps records the key. Deferred scroll props A deferred Scroll(...) prop reports "posts.data" , the same as a resolved one. This deliberately fixes a quirk in inertia-laravel: Testing See Testing for the full assertion API. Use deferred props for data the page can render without. If the page means nothing until the data arrives, a normal prop is simpler.

title: Typed routes
description: Generate a typed routes.ts for named endpoints, with typed parameters and request bodies, and write it at build time.
body: Typed routes give every named endpoint a typed function in routes.ts , with typed parameters and request bodies. This page builds on TypeScript types. The same o.TypeScript options write both files. Routes come from endpoint names, so they work the same whether an endpoint renders with Render("Component", props) or a page record. Generate routes.ts Set RoutesOutputPath , and every named endpoint gets a typed function in routes.ts . An endpoint gets its name from WithName , a controller route name, or a FastEndpoints Description(x = x.WithName(...)) : - Route parameters are typed from their constraints. Optional and catch-all parameters are optional. - Every HTTP method of an endpoint has a variant ( routes.users.update.put(1) ). - routeConfig.base prefixes every URL, for an app under a path base. - RouteBodies holds the [FromBody] (or FastEndpoints request) type of each route that has one. - Unnamed endpoints are skipped. o.TypeScript.LiveEvents(...) also exports live event names and channels as liveEvents . See Live props. To assert a route sent as a prop in tests, use WhereRoute(key, url, method) . See Testing. Generating at build time Set true in the project file. Every build, including the one inside dotnet publish , then runs the app once with --inertia-types to write both files. The app starts without listening on any port and exits. If the write fails, the build fails. In CI, compare the result with the committed files: Component names are checked at compile time too. See Page records. Instant visits Named MapInertia routes expose their component to the generated GET function. For a regular handler with one known destination, declare its final client component explicitly: The client shows the destination while the GET is pending. Let the page render a loading state until its page-specific data arrives. Use an ordinary link for conditional destinations. If a component transformer is configured, use explicit metadata only when you can declare the final name for that route.

title: Configuration
description: InertiaOptions, Vite, SSR, props, state and the middleware and result API.
body: Pass core configuration to AddInertia . Pass error page options to AddInertiaErrorPages . Options marked “Development only” do nothing in other environments. ComponentTransformer changes runtime component names only. If you use it, also register the final client names for TypeScript generation, because a build cannot evaluate an arbitrary runtime callback. AddInertia(o = ...) : InertiaOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- RootView "app.html" Root template path, relative to the content root. With UseRazorRootView , a Razor view name. Paths outside the content root are refused. RootElementId "app" Id of the root element and the data-page script. Version null Asset version. null means the Vite manifest hash, or "" without one. VersionResolver null Func that returns the version for each request. Takes priority over Version when non-null. ComponentTransformer null Changes the component name before rendering and page-file checks. Returning null keeps the name. EncryptHistory false Encrypt browser history state of every page. WithAllErrors false Send every validation message per field instead of the first. PreserveBigIntegers false Emit integers beyond ±(2^53−1) as {"$bigint":"..."} . ExposeSharedPropKeys true List top-level shared keys in sharedProps . CspNonce null Func : the request's CSP nonce. ConvertExternalRedirects true Turn an Inertia redirect to another origin into 409 + X-Inertia-Location . UrlResolver null Func : the page url . Pages.Directory / Pages.Extensions null / .tsx .jsx .ts .js .vue .svelte Development check that a rendered component has a page file. TypeScript.OutputPath , .Page (component) , .SharedProps () , .FlashData () null TypeScript declarations, written in Development. Share(key, value) / Share(key, Func ) none Shared props. o.Pagination : PaginationOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- DefaultPerPage 20 Default page size. MaxPerPage 100 Maximum page size. Must be below int.MaxValue to allow over-fetching. The default page size must be between 1 and this value. MaxPage null The last numbered page a bound PageRequest may fetch. A page beyond it is empty and runs no query or count. null means no ceiling. PageName "page" Numbered-page query parameter. PerPageName "perPage" Page-size query parameter. CursorName "cursor" Cursor query parameter. o.Vite : ViteOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- PublicDirectory "wwwroot" Web root containing the build directory and hot file. BuildDirectory "build" Vite output directory under PublicDirectory . Also the URL prefix. ManifestPath null Manifest path relative to the content root. null means {PublicDirectory}/{BuildDirectory}/.vite/manifest.json , then manifest.json . HotFilePath null Hot file path relative to the content root. null means {PublicDirectory}/hot . Read in Development only. DevServerUrl null Dev server origin, for example http://localhost:5173 . When set, dev tags always render. AssetBaseUrl null Replaces {PathBase}/{BuildDirectory} as the URL prefix of built assets. Prefetch None Waterfall or Aggressive : prefetch code-split chunks after load. PrefetchConcurrency 3 Chunks Waterfall downloads at a time. o.Ssr : SsrOptions Ssr.ConnectTimeout limits how long opening a connection may take, separately from the rendering deadline. The default is five seconds. Use a positive supported duration or Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan . Option Default Description --- --- --- Mode Disabled Disabled , Preferred or Required . Disabled cannot be overridden per response. OnRenderFailed null Thread-safe Action called once for the final failed render attempt, before fallback or a Required-mode exception. Urls empty ( http://127.0.0.1:13714 ) SSR server base URLs. Not used with UseNodeProcess() . Timeout 5 s Total deadline per render. Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan disables it. MaxResponseBytes 16 MiB Limit on actual response bytes, including errors and chunked responses. MaxPageBytes 2 MiB Pages whose JSON is larger render on the client without a call. BundlePath null Skip SSR while this file is missing, unless the Vite dev server runs. ExcludePaths empty Request paths never rendered on the server (exact, or a trailing for a prefix). Concurrency.MaxActive 8 Renders in flight per server from this app instance. 0 means no limit. Concurrency.MaxQueued 32 Renders waiting for a slot per server. Concurrency.QueueTimeout 250 ms How long a render waits for a slot. CircuitBreaker.Enabled true Pause servers that keep failing. CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold 5 Consecutive failures that open a server's circuit. CircuitBreaker.BreakDuration 10 s How long an open circuit skips the server before one probe. Cache.Duration Zero (off) Reuse a render for this long when the page JSON is the same. Cache.StaleFor Zero Serve stale while re-rendering. Cache.MaxBytes 64 MiB Size of the default store's render cache. UseNodeProcess(configure?) off Start and supervise Node SSR processes. Sets Mode = Preferred when the mode is Disabled . To set SSR for one response, use Render(...).WithSsr(SsrMode) or .WithoutSsr() . The full SSR options are in Server-side rendering. o.Props : InertiaPropsOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- MaxConcurrency 4 Loaders marked .Parallel() that run at once per render. Must be positive. CacheMaxBytes null Size of the default store's cached props. When set, cached props go in a private cache and the least recently used are evicted. null keeps them in the app's IMemoryCache without a bound of their own. o.State : InertiaStateOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- CookieName ".Inertia.State" Cookie name (cookie store) or session key (session store). RememberPreviousUrl false Remember successful page GET URLs for Back() when Referer is unavailable. RememberPartialReloads false Also remember same-component partial reload URLs when previous-URL tracking is enabled. Non-Inertia AJAX, prefetch and Precognition requests remain excluded. PreviousUrlCookieName ".Inertia.Previous" Plain previous-URL cookie, used with either state store. Must be non-empty and different from CookieName . CookieSecurePolicy SameAsRequest When state and previous-URL cookies are Secure . UseSession() off Use ISession instead of the encrypted cookie. AddInertiaMvc(o = o.UseTempDataStateStore()) off Use MVC TempData. Requires the Inertia.Net.Mvc package. AddInertiaErrorPages(o = ...) : InertiaErrorPagesOptions Option Default Description --- --- --- Component "Error" Default error component. Components empty Per-status overrides, with keys in StatusCodes . StatusCodes [403, 404, 500, 503] Non-empty set of statuses from 400 to 599. Protocol 409 and antiforgery 419 responses are preserved. EnabledInDevelopment false Preview error components in Development. Props null Func for additional props. See Error pages for setup, shared props and existing exception middleware. Middleware and endpoint API API Description --- --- services.AddInertia(configure?) Registers services and options. services.AddInertiaErrorPages(configure?) / app.UseInertiaErrorPages(useExceptionHandler: true) Error page services and middleware. Call the middleware before UseInertia() . Pass false when you use your own UseExceptionHandler() . app.UseInertia() The protocol middleware. Call it before the endpoints, and after UseSession() when used. app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(configure?) Issues the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and validates unsafe requests ( 419 on failure). app.MapInertia(pattern, component, props?) GET and HEAD endpoint that renders the component. services.AddInertiaDevTools(configure?) / app.MapInertiaDevTools() DevTools recorder and read API. Inertia.Net logs a warning when recording is enabled outside Development without an Authorize callback. The read API then returns 404. app.UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN") Only writes the token cookie. You validate the token yourself. endpoint.WithInertiaValidation() Minimal API: validation failures redirect back with errors. endpoint.WithInertiaPrecognition() Minimal API: WithInertiaValidation() plus Precognition. healthChecks.AddInertiaSsr(...) SSR health check from the gateway's state. mvc.AddInertiaMvc(o = o.UseRazorRootView("App")) MVC filter, optional Razor root view and component resolver. config.ConfigureInertia(configure?) FastEndpoints: validation redirect and Precognition. Render(component, props?) InertiaResult : .WithStatusCode , .WithRootView , .WithViewData , .WithSsr , .WithoutSsr , .WithSsrCache . Location(url) InertiaLocationResult . Back(fallback = "~/") InertiaBackResult : .WithErrors , .WithFlash . httpContext.Inertia() InertiaFeature : Share , Flash , WithErrors , ClearHistory , EncryptHistory , PreserveFragment . Send.InertiaAsync(...) , Send.InertiaLocationAsync(...) , Send.InertiaBackAsync(...) FastEndpoints Send extensions. Extension points - IInertiaRootView - IInertiaStateStore - ViteAssets - InertiaRequest (parsed headers) - InertiaHeaders (header name constants) - InertiaSsrException - InertiaSsr.HttpClientName (the SSR HTTP client) - InertiaDiagnostics (meter and activity source names) Name collisions The package imports Inertia.Net and static members of Inertia.Net.Inertia when implicit usings are enabled. If a name such as Location collides with a type, use Inertia.Net.Inertia.Location(url) . To manage imports yourself, set false in the project and add using Inertia.Net; and using static Inertia.Net.Inertia; where needed. InertiaPropJsonConverter , InertiaSsrHealthCheck , InertiaCacheEntryKind , InertiaCacheEntryOptions , InertiaPagesOptions , InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(...) and InertiaPrecognitionMetadata are public APIs for serialization, health checks, cache stores, page checks and precognitive request handling.

title: Redis cache
description: Share cached props and SSR renders between app instances with the Inertia.Net.Redis cache store.
body: Inertia.Net.Redis keeps cached props ( .Cache(...) ) and SSR renders in Redis. Every app instance shares them, and a call to IInertiaCache.RemoveByTagAsync on one instance clears them for all instances. Inertia.Net reads a page's cached props from Redis together, not one round trip after another. The loaders of those props still run in turn unless you mark them Parallel() . The default prefix is inertia.net: . How entries are stored - Each entry is a Redis string with the entry's expiration. Each tag is a set of entry keys that lives as long as its longest entry, and each entry keeps an index of its tags. - Storing or removing an entry is one script. When a removal races a store, the entry ends up either removed, or whole and still tagged. - Removing a tag works in batches, so a tag on every entry does not block the server. Put a hash tag in the prefix ( {myapp}: ), because an entry, its index and its tag sets change together in one script. Failures Inertia.Net does not hide failures. When the store fails while a page renders, Inertia.Net logs the failure (rate-limited) and renders without the cache. The loaders run, as on a cache miss. IInertiaCache calls throw, so a failed invalidation is not silent. Native AOT The Redis store is not verified under Native AOT. See the package README and Deploying behind a proxy for the rest of the multi-instance setup.

title: Head tags
description: Set the page title, meta and link tags on the server, in the first HTML response and on every visit.
headings: A title template and per-request tags
body: Set the page's , meta and link tags on the server. The tags are in the first HTML response. No JavaScript is needed, so crawlers and link previews see them. The tags are also sent with every visit as the head prop. A title template and per-request tags On the client Put @inertiaHead (or in Razor) before the template's own . See the root template. How tags are keyed - Values are HTML-encoded. - Each tag is keyed ( data-inertia ) by title , the meta name or property, or the link rel. A later call with the same key replaces the tag. Remove(key) removes a tag that was set earlier, for example by middleware. - With SSR the server-rendered head is used, which the client builds from the same prop. - o.Head.PropName renames the prop. In tests, HasHead("title", "Users - App") asserts a tag. See Testing.

title: Pages and responses
description: Render components, use MapInertia, and understand the root template and response status codes.
body: An Inertia page is a component name plus a set of props, the data that the component receives. The server writes this page object into the response. The client resolves the component and renders it. Rendering a page Render(component, props) returns an InertiaResult . The component name must match your client-side page resolver exactly, including case. Render accepts the props in one of these forms: - An InertiaProps , which is an ordered string-keyed dictionary. - Any IDictionary . - A typed object whose properties are the props. Nested InertiaProps and dictionaries are walked at any depth. This is the default style, and the rest of these docs use it. If you want typed props, use a record that implements IInertiaPage . The record names its component, so Render(new UsersPage(...)) needs no component string. The record can also hold its own GET handler. See Page records. Every page has an errors prop. It is an empty object when there are no errors. The key order is errors , shared props, then page props. Every response is one of three things, depending on how the request arrived: Per-response options InertiaResult has methods that change one response without changing the component: Method Effect --- --- .WithStatusCode(int) Sets the HTTP status of the page response .WithRootView(string) Uses another root template for this response .WithViewData(key, value) Makes a value available to @viewData("key") .WithSsr(SsrMode) / .WithoutSsr() Overrides the server-side rendering (SSR) mode for this response .WithSsrCache(duration, staleFor?) Reuses a server-rendered response for the same page JSON Pages without a handler MapInertia maps GET and HEAD to a rendered page, like Laravel's Route::inertia : The root template On the first visit the response is an HTML document. Inertia.Net reads app.html from the content root. You can change the file with RootView . Inertia.Net parses the template once and replaces these tokens: Token Output --- --- @inertia Without SSR: the page JSON script and the root element. With SSR: the server-rendered body. Required. @inertiaHead The SSR head tags joined with newlines. Empty without SSR. @vite("resources/js/app.tsx") Vite tags for one or more comma-separated entries. @viteReactRefresh The React Fast Refresh preamble while the dev server runs. Put it before @vite . @viewData("title") An HTML-encoded value passed with WithViewData . @@ A literal @ . Inertia.Net leaves other @ characters alone, such as CSS at-rules and e-mail addresses. Token arguments accept single or double quotes. The page JSON is escaped with \uXXXX sequences, so a prop containing cannot break out of the script element. An example app.html : RootElementId changes both the root element id and the data-page value. The default is app . The client finds the page script by that id. Inertia.Net reads app.html from disk at runtime. Add CopyToOutputDirectory and CopyToPublishDirectory so the file is present after dotnet publish . Razor root view (MVC) With Inertia.Net.Mvc , the first-visit HTML can be a Razor view: "App" finds Views/Shared/App.cshtml . The view receives an InertiaRootViewContext model and uses tag helpers: takes comma-separated entries. SSR runs at most once per request, and and share the result. WithRootView("Other") takes Razor view names when the Razor root view is enabled. A custom root view Implement IInertiaRootView and register it before AddInertia : Page URL and path base The page object's url is the request PathBase, Path and QueryString. If your app runs behind a proxy that rewrites paths, set o.UrlResolver to return the URL that the browser sees: Back() and the Vite asset URLs also respect the path base.

title: Installation
description: Install Inertia.Net, the optional MVC, FastEndpoints, SignalR, Redis or MongoDB package, and the testing helpers.
body: Inertia.Net is split into small packages. Install the core package and one optional backend integration. Package Install when --- --- Inertia.Net always. The core adapter, Minimal API support, Vite, server-side rendering (SSR), state store and antiforgery Inertia.Net.Mvc you use MVC controllers: ModelState filter, Razor root view and tag helpers Inertia.Net.FastEndpoints you use FastEndpoints: Send extensions, validation pre-processor and Precognition Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR you deliver live props over SignalR: hub, channel authorization and broadcaster Inertia.Net.EntityFrameworkCore you page EF Core queries with numbered or cursor pagination Inertia.Net.Redis you share cached props and SSR renders between app instances through Redis Inertia.Net.MongoDB you page MongoDB finds with numbered or cursor pagination Inertia.Net.Testing in your test project: fluent assertions over Inertia responses Inertia.Net.Templates you want to start from a complete app. Install it with dotnet new install Inertia.Net.Templates Use the same version for every Inertia.Net package. The package version and the Inertia.js protocol version are separate numbers: Inertia.Net 1.9.8 implements Inertia.js v3. Requirements - .NET 10 or .NET 11 SDK and a Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web project. - JavaScript frontend build tools with npm, Bun, pnpm or Yarn. Managed SSR requires Node.js or Bun at runtime. - An Inertia.js v3 client: @inertiajs/react , @inertiajs/vue3 or @inertiajs/svelte . .NET 10 and .NET 11 Every package ships net10.0 and net11.0 assemblies. NuGet picks the one that matches your app. On .NET 11, keep these points in mind: - Use 1.8.0 or later on .NET 11. Inertia.Net 1.7.1 and earlier were built against .NET 10 only. .NET 11 changed the experimental resolver API of Microsoft.Extensions.Validation . Because of that change, WithInertiaValidation() and WithInertiaPrecognition() from 1.7.1 fail on .NET 11 with TypeLoadException: Could not load type 'Microsoft.Extensions.Validation.IValidatableInfo' . - Retarget, don't roll forward. A net10.0 app that calls AddValidation() fails when it runs on the .NET 11 runtime ( DOTNET ROLL FORWARD=LatestMajor ). It fails whatever adapter it uses, because the validation source generator wrote .NET 10 types that .NET 11 removed. To fix it, set net11.0 and rebuild. - Dependencies follow the target framework. On net11.0 , Inertia.Net.EntityFrameworkCore depends on EF Core 11 and Inertia.Net.FastEndpoints depends on FastEndpoints 9. On net10.0 they use EF Core 10.0.15 and FastEndpoints 8.3.0. Reference the FastEndpoints.Generator version that matches your FastEndpoints version. - Async validators. Errors from AsyncValidationAttribute and IAsyncValidatableObject go through WithInertiaValidation() and WithInertiaPrecognition() in the same way as synchronous errors. See Validation and errors. - Automatic CSRF check. Apps built with WebApplication.CreateBuilder also get the framework's Sec-Fetch-Site / Origin check. UseInertiaAntiforgery() is still the token check Inertia needs. See CSRF and antiforgery. - C 15 unions work as props and in the generated TypeScript. See Props and TypeScript. - Compression. AddResponseCompression() also offers Zstandard and always adds Vary: Accept-Encoding . Inertia's Vary: X-Inertia stays next to it. Start from the template For another client, choose --framework vue or --framework svelte . For cookie sign-in, add --auth (see Authentication). The template includes working pages, a Todos form, validation, flash messages, CSRF protection and Vite configuration. The template's client has lint (oxlint), format and format:check (oxfmt) scripts. The build script type-checks first. Outside Development the app redirects to HTTPS and sends HSTS. The app targets .NET 10 (LTS) by default. To target .NET 11, add --tfm net11.0 . Install dependencies, then start Vite. Use the package manager you chose for your app. All four are supported: Package manager Install dependencies Start Vite Build assets --- --- --- --- npm npm install npm run dev npm run build Bun bun install bun run dev bun run build pnpm pnpm install pnpm run dev pnpm run build Yarn yarn install yarn run dev yarn run build Keep Vite running and start ASP.NET Core in another terminal with dotnet watch . For production, run the build command from your row of the table, then run dotnet publish -c Release . Keep the lockfile for the package manager you choose. Namespace and global usings The namespace is Inertia.Net and the static factory class is Inertia.Net.Inertia . C resolves a leading Inertia to the namespace, so Inertia.Render(...) does not compile outside the Inertia.Net namespace. The package's buildTransitive props file adds both global usings below when enable is set. That setting is the default in new projects. With these usings, you write Render(...) , Defer(...) , Once(...) , Back() and Location(...) without a namespace or class prefix. Set false and add using static Inertia.Net.Inertia; yourself, or call Inertia.Net.Inertia.Render(...) . HttpContext.Inertia() is an extension method and works as written. Next steps Add the four pieces every Inertia app needs: services, middleware, a root template and a client. Install React, Vue or Svelte and configure Vite for development and production.

title: TypeScript types
description: Generate declarations for page props, shared props and flash data from your .NET contracts.
body: Inertia.Net can write TypeScript declarations for typed page props, shared props and flash data. The declarations follow the app's JSON contracts, which are the HTTP JSON options and their source-generated contexts. As a result, names, nullability and enum values match the page JSON. To name a page's component once, see Page records. To generate a typed routes.ts for your named endpoints, see Typed routes. Configure generation Inertia.Net writes the file when the app starts in Development, and only when the content changed. Commit the file so that tsc passes in CI without running the app. Generate in CI To write the file without starting the app for real, for example in CI or outside Development, run the app with --inertia-types . The app writes the declarations in any environment and then stops. It exits with code 1 if it could not write them. The templates add this command as a script: Program.cs still runs up to app.Run() , so startup code such as migrations runs too. The server stops as soon as it has started. Shared props Inertia.Net infers shared props from the values passed to o.Share(...) . Dot keys nest. A factory is typed by what it returns. For example, o.Share("user", ctx = new UserDto(...)) gives user: UserDto . A factory cast to Func is unknown . Shares added per request (middleware, HttpContext.Inertia().Share(...) ) are not known at startup. Type them with o.TypeScript.SharedProps () , which replaces the inference with an explicit type. The InertiaConfig augmentation types usePage().props and flash . Flash data FlashData () types the whole flash object, not one entry. Each property of T is a flash key. To type Flash("toast", new Toast("success", "Saved")) , wrap the entry: Prop members An InertiaProp member is optional, because it can be deferred, optional or rescued. Its type is unknown , unless [InertiaPropType(typeof(T))] names its value type. Mapping .NET TypeScript --- --- int , long , double , decimal , float number ( number \ bigint for 64-bit and larger with PreserveBigIntegers ) DateTime , DateTimeOffset , DateOnly , TimeOnly , Guid , byte[] string enum union of JSON values. The values are numbers by default, with the member names in a doc comment. They are string names with JsonStringEnumConverter . dictionary Record polymorphic type union tagged with its discriminator C 15 union (.NET 11) union of its case types, User \ Team (plus \ null when a case is nullable) nullable member T \ null Types missing from the JSON metadata are unknown , with a warning in the log. Under Native AOT, register them in your context. Number handling follows member settings, then type settings, then the global JSON options. Custom converter output is typed as unknown with a warning when its shape cannot be inferred. Props and MVC validation error keys use the HTTP JsonOptions . FastEndpoints error keys use its binding serializer policy. Keep client field names aligned with the applicable policy. Custom resolvers without member metadata may require client JSON names for aliases.

title: Testing
description: Fluent assertions over Inertia responses and helpers for partial reloads and deferred props.
headings: Check page files and large integers
body: Inertia.Net.Testing has Laravel-style fluent assertions over Inertia responses and HttpClient helpers. It parses both JSON responses ( X-Inertia: true ) and the first-visit HTML . It also decodes $bigint values. A failed assertion throws InertiaAssertionException with a readable message, so the package works with any test framework. Check page files and large integers By default, Component("Users/Index") checks only the returned component name. To also check that the page file exists, use this fragment inside a test: React, Vue and Svelte extensions are allowed by default. Change PageExtensions to narrow that list. Component("Users/Index", false) skips the file check. Passing true forces it. When the page enables preserveBigIntegers , Where and HasFlash compare $bigint markers as integers, including nested values. The raw page stays unchanged. Without that flag, markers remain ordinary objects. A complete test class looks like this: Add public partial class Program; to your app when it uses top-level statements. To check that an error page keeps its HTTP status, use Status with the response's page assertion: Test host recipe With WebApplicationFactory , pin the asset version so that requests need no first visit to learn it. Also turn SSR (server-side rendering) off so that tests need no Node server: For form posts, read the XSRF token from a page response with GetXsrfToken() and send it with WithXsrfToken() . See Testing a form with antiforgery. A client that keeps cookies holds the antiforgery cookie and the sign-in cookie between requests. Create one with factory.CreateClient(new() { AllowAutoRedirect = false, HandleCookies = true }) . Request helpers Helper Purpose --- --- InertiaGetAsync(url, version?, configure?) Sends an Inertia GET InertiaRequestAsync(method, url, content?, version?, configure?) Sends an Inertia request with any method GetInertiaPageAsync() Parses the response into an InertiaPage AssertInertiaAsync(assert) Parses, runs the assertions and returns the page Page assertions The page assertions are: - Component , Url and Version . - HasFlash(key) , HasFlash(key, value) and MissingFlash(key) . - HasDeferred(path) and HasDeferred(group, path) . - HasLive(path) and HasLive(path, channel, event) for live props. Write the channel as "{type}:{name}" , for example private:orders.1 . - HasHead(key) or HasHead(key, contains) for head tags. The key matches the tags' data-inertia attribute: title , a meta name or property, or a link rel. For example: Prop assertions These assertions work on props and nested scopes. Keys can use dot paths and array indexes: Has(key) , Has(key, count) , Has(key, scope) , Has(key, count, firstItemScope) , HasAll , HasAny , Missing , MissingAll , Where(key, value) , Where(key, predicate) , WhereNot , WhereNull , WhereNotNull , WhereType(key, "string null") , WhereAllType , WhereContains(key, ...) , Count , CountBetween , Each(scope) , First(scope) and Dump() . WhereRoute(key, url, method) asserts a route sent as a prop in the client's { url, method } shape. The generated routes.ts functions return that shape. The method defaults to get , and the comparison ignores case: Strict interaction tracking. Like Laravel, a nested scope fails when it contains properties you did not assert, unless you end the scope with Etc() . The root scope is not checked automatically. Call .Interacted() at the end to require that every top-level prop was asserted. Partial reloads and deferred props InertiaPage replays the request with the right headers: HasScroll(path) asserts scroll metadata. HasScroll(path, currentPage, nextPage) also checks the page values. The next-page and previous-page helpers use the metadata and send the appropriate append or prepend intent. ReloadOnlyAsync asserts that "users" is in the result. ReloadExceptAsync asserts that "users" is missing. InertiaPage members Props , Raw , Prop(path) , HasProp(path) , PropBigInteger(path) , DeferredProps , MergeProps , PrependProps , DeepMergeProps , MatchPropsOn , RescuedProps , SharedProps , ScrollProps , OnceProps , LiveProps , Flash , EncryptHistory , ClearHistory , PreserveFragment , PreserveBigIntegers . Flash and errors travel in a cookie across the redirect, so use a client that keeps cookies. Disable AllowAutoRedirect to assert the redirect itself. Then follow the redirect with a second InertiaGetAsync to read the flash or errors. Testing a form with antiforgery Keep cookies and disable redirects on the test client. Then: 1. Load the form. 2. Send the form's XSRF token on the Inertia POST. 3. Follow the redirect. Import System.Net and System.Net.Http.Json . For a named error bag, use HasErrorBag("createUser") and HasError("email", bag: "createUser") . Dotted keys such as items.0.email are matched as flat error keys. With all errors enabled, a message assertion matches any message. GetXsrfToken() and WithXsrfToken() accept custom cookie and header names. The cookie container must keep the antiforgery cookie as well as the Inertia state cookie.

title: Pagination
description: Create numbered and cursor pages for pagers and infinite scroll.
headings: Project MongoDB lists into a DTO
body: A long list is easier to browse when the server sends a small group of items at a time. A numbered page lets readers choose a page. A cursor page uses a marker to fetch the next or previous group. Start with a list already in memory: A visit to /posts?page=2&perPage=5 returns the second group in posts.data . The default page size is 20 and the maximum is 100. Configure both in Pagination options. To stop at a last page, set MaxPage there. A page beyond MaxPage is empty and runs no query or count. For infinite scroll, wrap the page value in Scroll(...) and render it with InfiniteScroll , as shown in Infinite scroll. Pagination creates page values. Scroll adds infinite-scroll metadata and merging. Use a page directly for a classic pager. You write You get --- --- Pagination.Paginate(posts, request) A numbered Page for a pager Scroll(Pagination.Paginate(posts, request)) Numbered infinite scroll Scroll(await Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, key, fetch, ct: ct)) Cursor-based infinite scroll using your data source Scroll(ct = Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, fetch, ct: ct)).Defer() A deferred page. Other prop modifiers also work Minimal API handlers can take PageRequest or CursorRequest directly, as in Infinite scroll. MVC and FastEndpoints can call PageRequest.From(Request.Query) and CursorRequest.From(HttpContext) . Page numbers below 1 become 1. Invalid page sizes use the default, and sizes above the maximum are reduced to the maximum. Set defaults and parameter names with o.Pagination in AddInertia . From and BindAsync keep the query parameter name for the returned page. An explicit paginator name overrides that name. Pagination.Paginate slices an IReadOnlyList that is already in memory. For a database, search SDK or HTTP API, use Pagination.PaginateAsync . It accepts a fetch(skip, take, ct) delegate and an optional count delegate. It requests one extra item to determine hasMore . Without a count, total and lastPage are null. Delegate offsets above int.MaxValue return an empty page without calling fetch . The optional count still runs. Supply a stable, fully unique ordering to your data source. Pages do not contain URL links. For a classic pager, use currentPage , lastPage , and pageName to build links. from and to are one-based. Both are null on an empty page. The examples shorten the data array. For example, a data source can implement numbered pages without exposing IQueryable : For a pager, use Inertia links and preserve any other filters your app needs: Cursors A cursor is a marker for the position of an item. Cursors are useful when readers move forward and backward rather than jump to page numbers. The cursor overload of PaginateAsync takes a key selector and a fetch delegate. The delegate receives: - a decoded cursor with Direction ( After or Before ) and Value - a take count - a cancellation token Return rows in the requested direction, including up to one extra. The helper trims and reverses Before results to display order. Choose a stable, unique, non-null key. hasMore indicates that there are more rows in the requested direction. A cursor is the URL-safe base64 form of a compact JSON array: the direction ( "a" or "b" ) followed by the key values. Supported keys are int , long , Guid , string , DateTime , DateTimeOffset , decimal , double , and bool . Cursors are not tamper-proof . Apps that need tamper protection should wrap cursors with IDataProtector . A malformed or foreign nonempty cursor falls back to the first page. When CursorRequest.Logger is set, the paginator logs the fallback at Debug, without cursor values or exception details. Minimal API binding uses the configured pagination options. It also supplies a logger in the Inertia.Net.Pagination category when a logger factory is available. In MVC or FastEndpoints, CursorRequest.From(HttpContext) does the same. Optional arguments override the configured defaults and parameter names. For a query-only request or a request created outside HTTP, supply an app logger explicitly: Logger is ignored by JSON serialization and does not affect request equality. Defer or cache a page A page can use the same prop modifiers as other values. For example, Scroll(ct = Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, fetch, ct: ct)).Defer() loads the page after the first response. A lazy prop can also use .Cache(...) . See Deferred props and Props for loader and cache options. With EF Core If your app uses EF Core, install the optional package alongside your database provider: The following example uses an existing AppDb as db , with a Posts set. request is a PageRequest , cursorRequest is a CursorRequest , and ct is the request cancellation token: Both results contain the selected group in data . A cursor is a marker. Send it back unchanged to request the next or previous group. ToPageAsync requires an ordered query and counts rows by default. To skip the count, pass countTotal: false . Then total and lastPage are null. ToCursorPageAsync rejects a query that is already ordered. It orders by the supplied key and optional tie-breaker itself. Both guards throw InvalidOperationException . The cursor helper fetches in both directions without counting. Choose a stable, fully unique ordering. Use a unique key, or add a unique tie-breaker when the first key can repeat. Nullable keys are not supported. The cursor codec supports the types listed above, but EF translation and ordering for each type depend on the database provider. For example, SQLite needs a suitable value conversion to order DateTimeOffset . The corresponding page parameter uses the name from a bound request or From(...) . An explicit pageName or cursorName argument takes precedence. The EF Core package is not marked Native AOT compatible. EF Core has its own compiled-model requirements. For Native AOT applications, use the core delegate paginators with an AOT-compatible data source instead. With MongoDB Inertia.Net.MongoDB builds the same Page and CursorPage values from a collection.Find(filter) : The rules are the same as for the EF Core helpers: - ToPageAsync needs a sorted find. It replaces skip and limit, and counts the filter with CountDocuments unless you pass countTotal: false . - ToCursorPageAsync needs an unsorted find. It adds the keyset condition to the find's filter and sorts by the key (and tie-breaker). Keys may be ObjectId (held in the cursor as its 24-character string), int , long , string , Guid , DateTime , DateTimeOffset , decimal , double or bool . A tampered or unparseable cursor starts at the first page. - MongoDB orders strings by their UTF-8 bytes. The MongoDB driver does not support trimming or Native AOT, so neither does this package. See the package README. Native AOT Register each closed page type in your app's JsonSerializerContext along with the item types: See Native AOT. Caching and scroll props A cached page still writes its scroll metadata. Use cache keys that include the page or cursor and all user or tenant dependencies. Scroll(...) can be deferred or cached. Do not reuse its mutable prop instance across requests. You cannot combine root Append() and Prepend() on the same prop. See Props and Infinite scroll. Project MongoDB lists into a DTO Use ToProjectedPageAsync after Project when the view needs only a few fields. The sort and count still apply to the source query, and the page holds the projected type.

title: Why Inertia?
description: Build a C# backend for React, Vue or Svelte and see what Inertia.Net handles between them.
headings: From a C# route to a page
Inertia vs a SPA plus a Web API
When it is not a good fit
body: Coming from TypeScript? Keep React, Vue or Svelte and the frontend tools you know. Write your routes and business logic in C . The compiler checks your server code at build time. You can set a breakpoint in a C route and step through it as you click around the app. ASP.NET Core gives you routing, cookie sign-in and authorization in one web framework. When you add a database, Entity Framework Core lets you write queries in C and manage schema changes alongside the app. Inertia.Net can generate TypeScript types from your C page data and named routes. Change a field in C and your editor can show where the frontend needs to change. TypeScript types · Typed routes Already building in .NET? Keep your ASP.NET Core routes, controllers and validation rules. Add interactive pages in React, Vue or Svelte in the same project. The starter shows the whole workflow with a todo form. A C rule checks the title, and Inertia makes the error available beside the input. First 10 minutes From a C route to a page Your C handler chooses a frontend component and supplies its data. This route sends a list of users to the Users/Index page. The matching component receives users as a prop, the same way it receives data passed in by another component. On the first visit, Inertia.Net sends HTML. When someone follows an Inertia link, the server sends the next page's data as JSON and the browser updates the screen without a full reload. Inertia fits apps where the frontend and backend ship together, including dashboards, admin tools and SaaS products. If mobile apps or third parties also need access to your data, you can add API endpoints alongside your Inertia pages. How a request works The Inertia client sends the X-Inertia header when it requests a page in the background. Inertia.Net uses that header to send the page as JSON. Each route renders a page Data loading Fetch calls, loading states and caching in each component Props arrive with the page. Slow data can be deferred Authentication Tokens or cookies shared across two apps, plus client-side route guards Your normal ASP.NET Core cookie auth and [Authorize] Validation Return an error shape from the API and map it to forms in the client Redirect back with errors, available as form.errors (validation) API contract You design, version and document JSON endpoints The props you pass are the contract. TypeScript types can be generated Frontend React, Vue or Svelte React, Vue or Svelte You still write components, hooks and styles. What you no longer write is the connecting code: the API layer, the client router, and the code that keeps state in sync with the server. Features Area What you get Learn more --- --- --- Backends Minimal APIs, MVC controllers and FastEndpoints on one core package Quick start Clients React, Vue and Svelte with the Inertia.js v3 client Client setup Shared data Props sent with every page, such as the signed-in user, set statically or per request Shared data Validation Redirect back with errors before your handler runs, with named error bags Validation Precognition Validate a form before it is submitted, without running the handler Precognition Flash data One-time messages or typed values that survive a redirect Flash data Redirects and history Back() , Location() , external redirects, history encryption and clearing Redirects and history Error pages Routing failures and unhandled exceptions rendered as Inertia pages Error pages Asset versioning The client reloads once when your JavaScript or CSS changes Asset versioning Vite Manifest and dev-server tags, CDN base URLs, prefetching and CSP nonces Vite Server-side rendering Render the first visit on Node or Bun, supervised by the app, with a fallback to client rendering SSR CSRF The XSRF-TOKEN cookie and X-XSRF-TOKEN header, configured for you CSRF Multiple apps Mount a second Inertia UI under its own path with its own shared props and root view Mounts Native AOT Minimal API apps publish as Native AOT, using source-generated JSON metadata Native AOT TypeScript Generate declarations for page props, shared props and flash data from .NET types TypeScript types Testing Fluent assertions over Inertia responses, with helpers for partial reloads and deferred props Testing DevTools Record visits for the Inertia DevTools extension and catch missing page components DevTools Prop features Props are the data a page receives. Most of Inertia's performance and user-experience features are choices about how a prop is sent. Prop type In C What it does Learn more --- --- --- --- Plain ["title"] = "Hi" Sent on every response that includes the key Props Lazy Prop(() = ...) The loader runs only when the prop is part of the response Props Always Always(value) Sent even when a partial reload does not ask for it Partial reloads Optional Optional(() = ...) Never sent on the first visit, only when a partial reload asks for it Partial reloads Deferred Defer(() = ..., group: "stats") Left out of the first response, then loaded right away so the page shows up sooner Deferred props Merge Merge(value) , DeepMerge(value) The client appends or deep merges new data instead of replacing it Merging props Once Once(() = ...) Resolved once and remembered by the client, with optional expiry Once props Infinite scroll Scroll(page, ...) Merges pages of items and reports paging metadata Infinite scroll Rescued .Rescue() If its loader throws, the prop is left out and reported in rescuedProps instead of failing the whole page Props Parallel .Parallel() Starts independent async loaders together instead of one after another Props Cached .Cache(key, duration) Caches a loader's result between requests Props Live live props Refresh themselves when the server broadcasts an event, over SignalR or your own transport Live props Partial reloads let the client ask for only some props, with only and except . A filter change or a poll then does not recompute the whole page. See Pagination for the numbered and cursor pages that feed pagers and infinite scroll. When it is not a good fit - You need a public API anyway. Mobile apps, third-party integrations or several different clients need real JSON endpoints. You can build those next to your Inertia pages, but Inertia will not replace them. - The frontend is a separate product. If another team deploys the frontend on its own schedule, a versioned API is the cleaner boundary. - Heavy offline use. Inertia expects the server for every page change. - You want no JavaScript at all. For server-rendered HTML with a little interactivity, Razor Pages or Blazor may be simpler. Next steps - First 10 minutes creates an app from the starter template and walks through a validated form. - Quick start adds Inertia.Net to an existing ASP.NET Core app. - Introduction summarizes what the adapter provides.

title: Error pages
description: Render routing failures and unhandled exceptions as Inertia pages, with shared props and the original status.
body: When someone visits a missing page or the server encounters an error, you can show a page from your app instead of a blank response. Add this setup in Program.cs for production: A second Inertia UI mounted under its own path registers its own components with AddInertiaErrorPages(name, ...) . See Multiple apps and libraries. Create the named components in your client pages directory. Each component receives: - status - the values from the optional Props callback - shared props registered globally or through context.Inertia().Share(...) The Props callback receives the exception for exception responses and null for status-code pages. Avoid returning exception messages or stack traces to the client. Set o.IncludeSharedProps = false to omit configured/request shared props and shared head tags from these error pages. The errors prop and explicit error-page props (including status ) remain available. For example, ClientApp/pages/Error.tsx ( Error.vue for Vue, Error.svelte for Svelte): The handler answers requests with X-Inertia or an Accept: text/html navigation. It preserves the error status. An XHR receives a JSON page with X-Inertia: true . The first visit receives the normal root template. Root views and SSR work as for any other render. When SSR is enabled, an error component must also resolve in your SSR bundle. Only configured error statuses with an empty response are replaced. These are left to their existing handlers: - API clients - existing response bodies - redirects - Inertia's 409 responses - antiforgery's 419 responses Exceptions use the status selected by ASP.NET Core's exception middleware, which is 500 by default. The default statuses are 403, 404, 500 and 503. Extend StatusCodes to handle other error statuses. A page explicitly returned with Render(...).WithStatusCode(404) keeps its component and props. In Development, error pages are disabled so the developer exception page and Inertia debug modal stay available. Set o.EnabledInDevelopment = true to preview your error components. The Inertia client renders non-2xx Inertia responses by default. Application httpException event handlers or onHttpException callbacks can cancel that rendering. Already using UseExceptionHandler() AddInertiaErrorPages() registers an IExceptionHandler in the existing chain. Register API-specific handlers first if they should take priority. Use one exception middleware. Then install only the status-code part: ASP.NET Core 10 suppresses exception diagnostics by default when an IExceptionHandler handles the exception. The Inertia handler follows that policy and emits only a Debug message naming the rendered component. To keep the built-in exception logs and diagnostics, configure the exception middleware explicitly: AddInertiaErrorPages() also registers the built-in ProblemDetails service as the exception middleware’s fallback. The Inertia exception handler declines requests that do not ask for an Inertia page or HTML, so API exceptions use the host’s ProblemDetails fallback and content negotiation. Existing ProblemDetails configuration and earlier application handlers still apply. Empty status-code responses remain unchanged. Loaded flash and validation state is consumed when an error page renders, as on any other page response. Validation, SSR and rate limits Validation redirects keep their existing behavior. The exception pipeline can handle a required SSR failure. Configure the error page so that it can render without relying on the same failed renderer. Rate-limit responses with an existing body are preserved. Configure the rejection response explicitly, including the Precognition header for validation requests. See Precognition.

title: CSRF protection
description: Protect forms with the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.
body: The Inertia client reads the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and sends its value as the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on every request. UseInertiaAntiforgery() issues that cookie and validates it, so one call protects every form. What it does - Issue. A page load gets the request token in a cookie. A page load is a GET or HEAD request that is an Inertia request or accepts text/html . The cookie is script-readable and essential: HttpOnly off, SameSite=Lax , Path=/ , Secure per SecurePolicy . Essential means a cookie-consent policy does not withhold it. - Validate. IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync checks every unsafe request. An unsafe request is anything but GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE. The check covers JSON bodies and form bodies, and Inertia requests and other requests. A plain cross-site HTML form post is rejected, and so is a forged XHR. UseInertiaAntiforgery() also sets the antiforgery feature, so form-binding endpoints work without app.UseAntiforgery() . - Reject. A request with a missing or wrong token gets 419 (page expired, as in Laravel). The handler does not run. - Opt out per endpoint with .DisableAntiforgery() , for example for webhooks and test hooks. Opt out for whole areas with ShouldValidate . .NET 11 automatic CSRF check Apps built with WebApplication.CreateBuilder on .NET 11 also get the framework's automatic CSRF middleware. That middleware checks Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin on unsafe requests, issues no tokens, and only records a verdict. UseInertiaAntiforgery() remains the token check Inertia needs. Like app.UseAntiforgery() , it replaces that verdict with its own. A request with a valid token passes, and a request without one still gets 419 . .DisableAntiforgery() opts an endpoint out of both checks. The configuration setting DisableCsrfProtection=true turns the automatic check off. Options OnRejected runs after UseInertia() . Returning Back() gives the tab a fresh token and a message instead of the client's error dialog. Lazy refresh By default, every page load issues a fresh token, and antiforgery marks that response Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store . That header also keeps the page out of the browser's back/forward cache. o.CookieRefresh = XsrfCookieRefresh.Lazy keeps a token that still validates. Responses that keep the token get no Set-Cookie and stay cacheable. A token issued before a sign-in or sign-out is replaced on the next page load. Validating a token costs about as much as issuing one, so the gain is in the responses, not in CPU. Set your own Cache-Control on pages with private data. A session that expires or a sign-in that changes the user invalidates the token in an open tab. The next page load issues a new token. Returning Back() from OnRejected gives that tab a fresh token and a message. MVC and FastEndpoints UseInertiaAntiforgery() covers controllers too. [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken] as a global filter still works, but is not needed. The middleware covers FastEndpoints as well. FastEndpoints' own EnableAntiforgery() is not needed for Inertia forms. Issue only UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN") is the 1.0 API. It only writes the cookie. You then validate in two places: app.UseAntiforgery() checks form bodies only, and your own check covers JSON bodies ( await antiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync(context) ). Prefer UseInertiaAntiforgery() . Troubleshooting 419 - Was the page loaded through the middleware? The middleware sets the cookie. - Does the cookie reach the browser? Secure cookies are dropped on plain HTTP. Behind a proxy that terminates TLS, configure forwarded headers or set CookieSecurePolicy.Always . - Do all instances share the Data Protection key ring? - Does UseAuthentication() run before the antiforgery middleware? - Did a sign-in or sign-out change the token? Reload the page, or use OnRejected . See Deploying for proxy and multi-instance settings.

title: Server-side rendering
description: Render the first visit on Bun or Node, supervise the process from .NET, and fall back safely.
headings: 3. Let the app run Bun or Node
body: Server-side rendering (SSR) renders the first visit on a JavaScript server, using your client bundle. Crawlers and slow devices then get HTML. Inertia XHR requests are never rendered on the server. 1. Build the SSR bundle With @inertiajs/vite The @inertiajs/vite plugin wraps the entry with the SSR server bootstrap and resolves your pages. The entry is ClientApp/ssr.tsx for React and ClientApp/ssr.ts for Vue and Svelte. Build both bundles: Without the plugin Write the server entry yourself ( ssr.tsx for React, ssr.ts for Vue and Svelte): The client entry hydrates the page when the server rendered it: Run the bundle with Bun or Node, or let the app start it: Build and run from a directory with node modules installed. The SSR build leaves node modules imports external. 2. Enable it A response can choose its own mode: The global mode decides first. When it is Disabled , SSR is off and no response can override that. Otherwise the response's mode wins, then ExcludePaths , then the global mode. SSR runs only for first visits, which are the HTML responses. Inertia.Net posts the page JSON to {url}/render . The answer, { "head": [...], "body": "..." } , is written into the root view. @inertiaHead outputs the head tags. @inertia outputs the body. 3. Let the app run Bun or Node A hosted service runs {Executable} {bundle} once per instance. The executable is node by default, and Bun works too. The service logs stdout as Information and stderr as Warning under Inertia.Net.Ssr . It waits for every instance's GET /health . Occupied ports are refused before anything is spawned. Ssr.Urls is not used in managed mode, where the app runs the SSR process. The executable is configurable. This documentation site builds a self-contained SSR bundle and runs it with Bun: o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess(n = n.Executable = "bun") . The default is node . The bundle accepts either runtime. - An instance that exits is restarted after 1 second. The delay doubles up to 30 seconds. - An instance that stops answering its liveness check is killed and restarted the same way. - Shutdown stops the owned process trees without requesting /shutdown . - Nothing is spawned while the Vite dev server runs. - For external or remote servers, set Mode and Urls without UseNodeProcess() . The SSR server has no authentication. Anyone who can reach it can POST /render , which uses CPU, or POST /shutdown . Its head and body are written into your pages verbatim. Listen on 127.0.0.1 . Before an instance takes renders, Inertia.Net tries the machine's non-loopback addresses on the instance's port. If the instance answers there, Inertia.Net stops it and logs an error. AllowNetworkExposure = true keeps the instance running with a warning. A graceful shutdown stops the SSR process. If the .NET process is killed outright, the OS does not stop the SSR runtime with it. Use a process manager or container for hard-crash cleanup. 4. Development When the Vite hot file is present (Development only), or o.Vite.DevServerUrl is set, Inertia.Net posts to {viteDevUrl}/ inertia ssr . @inertiajs/vite serves this endpoint, so you need no built bundle and no separate SSR server. Use ssr.ts as the entry for Vue and Svelte. BundlePath is ignored while the dev server runs. 5. Failures and fallbacks Send failures to monitoring Preferred mode logs a failed render and lets the browser render the page. Required mode fails the request before any HTML is sent. To send failures to monitoring, set the o.Ssr.OnRenderFailed callback during registration (fragment): The callback receives the error, type, hint, timestamp and any available stack or source information. It runs once for the final failed attempt, before the fallback or the Required-mode exception. Keep the callback thread-safe. Do not show these details to users, because renderer diagnostics may contain secrets. Policy skips, such as a missing bundle or an open circuit, use logs and metrics. In Preferred mode, every failure logs a warning and the page renders on the client. In Required mode, a failure throws InertiaSsrException before the first byte is written, so the app's exception handler can still answer. After enough failures in a row, the app stops calling the SSR server for a while. It then probes the server before trusting it again: Type Cause Opens the circuit --- --- --- connection Connection refused or reset. A refused connection is retried on another server. yes timeout Ssr.Timeout elapsed yes http Non-2xx answer without a structured error yes response Empty or malformed answer yes render The component threw (structured error from the renderer) no response-too-large Answer over MaxResponseBytes no overloaded No render slot within Concurrency.QueueTimeout , or the queue is full no circuit-open , not-ready , page-too-large , bundle-missing Skipped without a call no Circuit breaker. The circuit breaker counts consecutive failures of the types that open the circuit. After CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold of them (default 5), a server is skipped for BreakDuration (default 10 s). Then one render probes the server. If the probe succeeds, the circuit closes. If the probe fails, another break starts. A page that fails because of its own code never pauses the server. Render slots. Each server takes at most Concurrency.MaxActive renders at once from this app instance. The default is 8, and 0 means no limit. Up to MaxQueued more renders (default 32) wait for a slot, each for at most QueueTimeout (default 250 ms). Renders that find no slot fall back immediately. 6. Several servers Each render goes to a server whose circuit is closed: the one with the fewest renders in progress. Ties rotate. Every server has its own slots, queue and circuit. Only a refused connection is retried on another server, within the same deadline. Page props travel to the renderer, and the renderer's HTML goes into your pages unescaped. The renderer must therefore be trusted. A plain http:// URL that is not loopback logs a warning at startup. Use HTTPS or a private network. 7. Health check The health check reports what the renders have already shown. It does not call the SSR servers. It reports: - healthy while SSR is disabled, while SSR goes through the Vite dev server, or while every server can take renders - degraded while some circuits are open or some managed instances are not ready - the registration's failure status (default unhealthy) when no server can take renders The check's data lists each server's state. 8. Observability Instrument Type Tags --- --- --- inertia.page.duration (s) histogram inertia.response , inertia.partial inertia.page.size (By) histogram inertia.response inertia.ssr.duration (s) histogram inertia.ssr.outcome inertia.ssr.queue.duration (s) histogram inertia.ssr.active up-down counter inertia.ssr.outcomes counter inertia.ssr.outcome , inertia.ssr.reason inertia.ssr.response.size (By) histogram inertia.ssr.circuit.state gauge inertia.ssr.endpoint inertia.ssr.circuit.transitions counter inertia.ssr.endpoint , to inertia.ssr.process.restarts counter cause inertia.props.rescued counter Tag values are bounded: they contain no URLs, component names or user data. The inertia.render activity carries inertia.component . The inertia.ssr activity carries inertia.ssr.endpoint , inertia.ssr.outcome and inertia.ssr.reason . Nothing is recorded unless a listener is attached. 9. Response cache A render depends only on the page JSON. A page whose JSON is byte for byte the same for many visitors can reuse its HTML: The cache key is the SHA-256 of the page JSON (component, props, url, version and the rest). A new deploy or different props therefore never reuse a stale render. Pages with per-user props make one entry per user, so cache the pages that are shared. A cache hit is counted as inertia.ssr.outcomes{inertia.ssr.outcome=rendered, inertia.ssr.reason=cache} and bypasses the render slots and circuit breakers. Nothing is cached while the Vite dev server renders. Concurrent misses for the same page share one fill per app instance. Waiting counts against Ssr.Timeout . Cancelling a waiting request does not cancel the request that fills the entry. With StaleFor , a render past its Duration is still served. The bounded background worker refreshes it after the response completes, like stale props. The connection can accept its next request while the renderer runs. Refreshes cancel when the host stops. If the 64-entry queue is full, the refresh is dropped and logged. Monitor inertia.cache.refresh.dropped with inertia.cache.kind=ssr . IInertiaCache.ClearSsrAsync() removes every render. Ssr.ConnectTimeout limits the time to establish a connection, independently of Ssr.Timeout . Both accept a positive duration or Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan . In Required mode, InertiaSsrException.Message contains a generic failure category suitable for an error page. Renderer diagnostics remain in application logs and diagnostic exception properties. Do not expose those properties to clients. Connection timeout and cached renders Ssr.ConnectTimeout defaults to five seconds and limits the time to establish a connection. Ssr.Timeout limits the entire render. In Required mode, exceptions use a generic public message. Diagnostic properties can contain private renderer details, so do not display them to users. A stale SSR cache hit returns immediately and schedules a refresh on a bounded background worker. The worker's queue holds 64 pending refreshes. A dropped refresh logs a warning and increments inertia.cache.refresh.dropped with inertia.cache.kind=ssr . Cached prop loaders used with stale refresh must use singleton dependencies or create their own scope. Never capture request-scoped services or HttpContext . Global Ssr.Cache.Duration is suitable for anonymous pages. Prefer per-page WithSsrCache and keys that account for all user and tenant data.

title: Validation
description: Redirect back with validation errors for Minimal APIs, MVC and FastEndpoints, and add Precognition.
body: Inertia forms post, expect a redirect, and read validation errors from props.errors on the next page. Inertia.Net performs the redirect and carries the errors across it. - A field maps to its first message. With o.WithAllErrors = true a field maps to an array of all its messages. The client's form.withAllErrors() expects that array. - Error keys use dotted indices, for example items.0.email . A name uses the JSON member alias when metadata exposes one. Other members use the applicable naming policy. Dictionary keys are preserved. Minimal API and MVC use the page serializer’s HTTP JSON options. FastEndpoints uses its binding serializer policy. Two cases may fall back to naming-policy conversion: custom resolvers that omit member metadata, and paths without a model schema. Align field names and serializer settings. - Error bags. An error bag is a named group of errors. The client sends X-Inertia-Error-Bag: createUser when the form has errorBag="createUser" . Errors arrive as errors: { createUser: { email: "..." } } . Without the header, errors is the flat object { email: "..." } . A bag stored under a name other than default is always nested by bag name. Validation libraries Backend Validation --- --- Minimal API .NET 10 source-generated DataAnnotations through AddValidation() . ValidationProblem results. For FluentValidation, call IValidator yourself and return WithErrors . MVC MVC model validation and ModelState FastEndpoints FastEndpoints validators, including FluentValidation Minimal API WithInertiaValidation() applies to a route or route group. It requires services.AddValidation() . Without validation resolvers, WithInertiaValidation() throws InvalidOperationException when the endpoint is constructed. Routing may construct endpoints lazily, so the exception does not always appear during application startup. For an Inertia request that is not a GET, a validation failure becomes a redirect back with the errors. The redirect status is 303 for PUT/PATCH/DELETE/QUERY. Every other client still gets the normal 400 validation problem. Inertia.Net converts a handler result the same way when the handler returns TypedResults.ValidationProblem(...) , Results.ValidationProblem(...) or an HttpValidationProblemDetails . On .NET 11, async validators ( AsyncValidationAttribute , IAsyncValidatableObject ) report through WithInertiaValidation() and WithInertiaPrecognition() like synchronous attributes. A body that cannot be bound, such as malformed JSON, is still a 400 on both .NET 10 and .NET 11. It is never a redirect back without errors, and never a Precognition success. The built-in .NET 10 validation filter is added automatically and always runs outermost. It writes the 400 itself before any filter you add can see the failure. WithInertiaValidation() disables the built-in filter on the endpoint and runs the same source-generated validation itself. Do not combine WithInertiaValidation() with your own .DisableValidation() . To report errors yourself, without attribute validation: Back().WithErrors(IDictionary errors, string bag = "default") also takes arrays of messages. Minimal API AddValidation() does not run FluentValidation automatically. Call a registered IValidator yourself and map its failures: Import FluentValidation and register your validator. Use the client's JSON field names as the dictionary keys when they differ from the validator's property names. MVC AddInertiaMvc() registers a global filter. When an Inertia non-GET request has an invalid ModelState , the filter redirects back with the errors before the action runs. The errors go in the bag named by X-Inertia-Error-Bag . The default bag is default . [ApiController] controllers work too. For Inertia requests, the same redirect replaces their automatic 400. Binding failures get the generic message The value is invalid. , because their exception messages can expose internals. FastEndpoints c.ConfigureInertia() adds a global pre-processor. A validation failure of an Inertia non-GET request becomes a redirect back with the errors. Other requests keep FastEndpoints' 400 JSON. FluentValidation validators work as usual. c.ConfigureInertia() works together with an existing c.Endpoints.Configurator . The optional callback of c.ConfigureInertia() runs after Inertia setup. The Inertia pre-processor runs after an endpoint's own pre-processors. If one of those already answered, for example with a 403, its answer wins. Precognition (live validation) Precognition validates a request without running the handler. Minimal APIs use .WithInertiaPrecognition() instead of .WithInertiaValidation() . FastEndpoints enables Precognition with ConfigureInertia() . MVC does not support Precognition. Error bags in the client All errors for a field With the option on, errors.email is an array of every message instead of the first. State and redirects Validation errors travel in the state store across the redirect. By default the state store is an encrypted cookie. It can be a session or MVC TempData instead. See Flash data for the store choices and size limits.

title: Native AOT
description: Publish a Native AOT Inertia.Net app with source-generated JSON metadata.
body: You can publish an Inertia.Net app with Native AOT. Inertia.Net , Inertia.Net.FastEndpoints and Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR are annotated IsAotCompatible . CI publishes a real app with Native AOT ( tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke ) with zero trim and AOT warnings allowed. The library never reflects over your props. It writes values with JsonTypeInfo from your JsonSerializerContext . 1. Register a JSON context Register every prop type and chain the context into the HTTP JSON options: Register these in the context: - the type that each loader returns - each plain value you place in InertiaProps - flash values that are not plain strings or numbers The library's own context already covers string , bool , int , long , double , decimal , float , Guid , DateTime , DateTimeOffset , DateOnly , TimeOnly , TimeSpan , JsonElement , string[] , int[] , List , Dictionary , Dictionary , InertiaProps and Dictionary . The source generator accepts members of type InertiaProp without any attribute. 2. Make validation models public The .NET 10 AddValidation() source generator skips internal types. Validation of those types then does nothing and reports no error. Only one AddValidation() call site per project is allowed. 3. Add ProblemDetails The non-Inertia 400 validation problem needs the ProblemDetails JSON metadata, or it cannot be serialized without reflection. 4. Avoid anonymous types Anonymous types do not work as props, flash values or published live prop values under AOT. Use InertiaProps , records or classes registered in the context. Register the types you publish as live values in the same context. 5. Copy content files The app reads app.html and the Vite manifest from disk at runtime. Copy them to the publish directory. When the binary may run from another directory, set the content root to the binary's directory: In the project file: 6. Use Minimal APIs or FastEndpoints Inertia.Net.Mvc is not AOT compatible, because ASP.NET Core MVC itself is not. Use Minimal APIs or FastEndpoints. 7. FastEndpoints source generation DiscoveredTypes is generated by the FastEndpoints.Generator package, in the namespace named after the assembly. See samples/FastEndpoints.Svelte . 8. Trim HTTP/3 The SSR client never uses HTTP/3, so HTTP/3 support can be trimmed out: These features are all AOT safe and covered by the smoke test: - cached props - the SSR cache - nonces - prefetching - MapInertia - the DevTools recorder - live props over SignalR SignalR itself does not support strongly typed hubs ( Hub ) under AOT, so keep any hubs of your own untyped. Set JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false in regular builds too. A missing JsonSerializable registration then fails in tests instead of only in the AOT publish. The reference app is tests/Inertia.Net.AotSmoke/Program.cs . Run it end to end with bash eng/aot-smoke.sh on Linux with clang and zlib installed.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Common errors, their causes, and how to fix them.
headings: My 404 shows the Inertia modal in production
The Inertia page component was not found
A redirect to another site turns into a 409
The root view resolves outside the content root
The page keeps reloading, or a request loops with 409
The dev server tags do not appear
